dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: There's grain behind that door. I'm not asking whether there's enough to feed the entire station. I need four days for my patients.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: It belongs to people who paid me to keep it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The people downstairs can see it. You can't make that part of the arrangement invisible.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'm aware that stored grain has become a controversial decorative feature.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You could open the door yourself.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I could also sell the grain twice, get paid twice, and retire somewhere no one has ever heard of me. I don't do that either.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: It's a remarkably low standard of virtue you've set for yourself.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: It gets me out of bed.

sourceActionBeats: *VEIL MARKET. Jex stands on the upper balcony of his bonded stores. Below him, a ration hall is filling faster than its shutters can be opened. Naomi has brought an injured Shard caregiver seeking food for people who cannot stand in the queue.*

*The caregiver has been watching the little bargaining game without joining it. She takes a cracked inhaler casing from her bag. She doesn't offer it as evidence; she has simply forgotten to put it away.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: You keep talking about a door. When I'm downstairs, people ask me whether the patients are getting worse because I haven't tried hard enough. I tell them the medicine hasn't come. They say try another door. Another broker. Another captain. As if somebody's hiding the good door from us.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Sometimes someone is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Yes. That's the problem. I no longer know whether to believe that when a neighbor says it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know what you're asking. I'm trying to work out what I'll owe the people who already bought this consignment.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I'm asking if I can take four days of grain home before somebody dies. You can work out the bill afterward. I promise you I'll be just as poor when you finish.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Do you know what I did when the medicine stopped arriving? I divided each dose until it stopped being medicine. I don't want to do that to food.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Jex! Down!

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That was spectacularly rude.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Stop trying to be funny and hold pressure on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The two ambitions are not incompatible.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Somebody's going to get crushed. The people at the bottom don't know about the knife.

panelPlan: Jex looks away first. Naomi notices. Before he can answer, the caregiver continues.
She strikes the assailant aside, but the knife catches Jex. The attack sends people below running. A flare ignites a vendor row at precisely the.
Naomi presses a folded cloth into his hand. He can't hold it steady until she pins his wrist against the balcony rail. The caregiver looks down the staircase.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Get to the lower hall. Tell the workers to open the side lane. Don't tell them an assassin has arrived unless you want them to turn around and run into him.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That side lane's been closed for three weeks.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I know. I helped close it. The hinges were pulling out of the wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I had a report saying the mechanism was repaired.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Then you've discovered what reports are good for.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Are your patients down there?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Three of them. The fourth can't walk this far. I left a neighbor with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Go. I'll keep him alive long enough to argue about the door.

panelPlan: She starts toward the stairs. Naomi catches her sleeve.
Jex makes a weak sound that might have been a laugh. Then the first flare catches the vendor row and the balcony fills with hot, oily smoke. He stops.
He puts his hand on the wound and sees blood. It no longer seems an entertaining observation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET — FIRE / AURIC — CIVIC MEDICAL

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: We have a landing point. Medical personnel only. No Fleet patrols inside the market.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Our medics can come without a security detachment, but they need a clear route from the landing.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I'll get you one.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Open it. No levy. Tell them the releases are mine to authorize.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The buyers will make claims against you.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: They have my address. They've been using it enthusiastically for years.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: We can move the grain ourselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Then do. And if somebody starts a crush, tell them they will have to answer to me. I am told I'm very impressive when bleeding.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: Let the store open. Restrict the approaches. It will teach them what an unlicensed passage is worth.

panelPlan: Sera reaches Venn on a civilian emergency frequency. The Veil Market is burning; there are burn victims. Sera requests medics but refuses armed intervention..
Jex, wounded and stubborn, gives Naomi access to his bonded food reserve.
The Trade Mask cannot lawfully close Jex's private shutters. Its loyalists can block the streets.

settingText: VEIL MARKET — FIRE / AURIC — CIVIC MEDICAL

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The stores are bonded privately. We can stop the carts, but not the opening. There are hungry crews in our own sector. They'll see us stopping food from reaching them.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: They already see the broker presenting himself as the generous man who feeds them. His access must not become a competing government.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: One of the cart drivers served on my cousin's ship. They aren't supporters of Jex. They're taking home sacks.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: Then they can return to their kitchens and ask why a man who kept the grain for months has suddenly decided to release it. They should ask him who paid for the original shipment. They should ask him what happens when it is gone.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.

settingText: VEIL MARKET — FIRE / AURIC — CIVIC MEDICAL

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: And if they ask us why we blocked the street?

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE MASK
dialogueInline.text: Tell them it was my decision. I will answer for it. But keep the barrier away from the fire crews. We gain nothing by burning down the market we claim to govern.

dialogueInline.speaker: MEDIC
dialogueInline.text: We have supplies for burns and smoke exposure. There's no path through.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Don't force it. Ask Sera for the civilian route. We go where we've been invited, or we don't go.

dialogueInline.speaker: MEDIC
dialogueInline.text: People are hurt in there.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know. That doesn't give us permission to turn their market into a second battlefield.

panelPlan: Trade looks down at the movement of workers and civilians on the feed.
The emissary leaves to execute an order he knows the workers will hate. His limited concession about the fire crews will not keep the lanes clear.
At the Fleet medical landing, a medic faces the physical barrier.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET — JEX’S OFFICE

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Somebody paid for the knife and for empty-looking ration doors. These transactions are connected.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The connection isn't the explanation. People were hungry before the payments. You can't buy that with a single envelope.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't planning to call everyone down there a hired actor.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know. I keep hearing my own voice coming out as an argument with people who haven't made the accusation.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You should be with the medics.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Every road to the medics seems to go through a door I own. And I'm beginning to think that's part of why someone's trying to kill me.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Has Tali answered?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You checked twice while I was here.

panelPlan: Naomi returns to Jex's office with the assassin's payment chit and legitimate cargo records. The amount matches a sequence of freight diversions, but the.
Naomi glances at the bandage across his side. He looks worse than he did half an hour ago.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Naomi returns to Jex's office with the assassin's payment chit and legitimate cargo records. The amount matches a sequence of freight diversions, but the signatures are indirect.*
*Naomi glances at the bandage across his side. He looks worse than he did half an hour ago.*

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't telling you to stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If I break that seal, I lose a route I've spent fifteen years building.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: If you don't break it, the fire crews will have to turn back through the food queue.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I'm told you're the man who can open any door.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'm very much a man who can purchase the services of someone with a larger cutting tool.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Good. Stand back.

He presses the release. The door doesn't move. The caregiver brings a cutter.
The passage opens. Jex does not pretend the rescue has solved his wound, the shortages or the contractual damage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — MARKET / CIVIC MEDICAL

dialogueInline.speaker: STAFF
dialogueInline.text: There's nowhere else to put the wounded.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: There are people living behind those screens. Some cannot be moved. Clear the freight aisle, bring beds in from the empty storage room, and ask for volunteers who can walk. Don't start by throwing out the people who happen to be nearest the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: STAFF
dialogueInline.text: The storage room has no working heater.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: The burn victims need treatment first and heat next. Put the triage beds on the warm side of the aisle. We can ask the people already here whether they are able to move their bedding.

panelPlan: Auric. Halev is at the market, while Sera receives incoming burn victims. She is asked to evict people already sheltering in the receiving hall to make space.
A resident who has heard the exchange emerges from behind one of the screens.

sourceActionBeats: *Auric. Halev is at the market, while Sera receives incoming burn victims. She is asked to evict people already sheltering in the receiving hall to make space.*
*A resident who has heard the exchange emerges from behind one of the screens.*

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: My husband can't stand without help. You're not moving him to an unheated room because you're afraid to tell the medics you have nowhere to put them.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I'm not asking you to move him.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: That's what they said yesterday. Then somebody came with a form.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Put the form down. Tell me what your husband needs.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: A chair with arms. And the same nurse, if you can manage it. He gets frightened when new people lift him.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: We can manage a chair. Find the nurse. And when the ambulances arrive, don't promise the patients a bed you haven't prepared.

dialogueInline.speaker: STAFF
dialogueInline.text: You know they'll blame us for the delay.

panelPlan: Sera turns to the staff member, who has been waiting for a decision he can enter on a schedule.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Sera turns to the staff member, who has been waiting for a decision he can enter on a schedule.*

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: They can blame me. You're the one who has to carry the bed.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: These belong to customers. We could move them piece by piece.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: How long?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Forty minutes, maybe more.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Then take the cutter. I'll tell the customers what happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: You'll owe them.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Yes. It seems an appropriate day for debts.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: We might get through one bay before the battery dies. After that we need a second cutter.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Where's the second cutter?

panelPlan: The fire reaches Jex's bonded storeroom. The open food crates slow the rescue crews. He authorizes workers to cut through merchandise to create an aisle.
The worker examines the cutter. Its battery pack is barely large enough for the first shelf of reinforced casing. Behind the merchandise, smoke has begun.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The fire reaches Jex's bonded storeroom. The open food crates slow the rescue crews. He authorizes workers to cut through merchandise to create an aisle.*
*The worker examines the cutter. Its battery pack is barely large enough for the first shelf of reinforced casing. Behind the merchandise, smoke has begun spilling from the ceiling joint.*

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: In the lockup you leased to a merchant who hasn't paid us in six months.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That sounds like an unfortunate administrative arrangement. I'll have a conversation with myself about it later.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: You can't make a passage through the shelves by signing a release. Somebody has to be standing here holding the tool.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I can't hold it. Tell me where you need people, and I can get them here.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: You're injured. Go sit down.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If I sit down, I'll hear the buyers complaining before the smoke gets to them. Neither of us deserves that.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: The barrier is still there. We can remove it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: We have a usable route. Send the medics through it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: It will take longer.

panelPlan: Jex looks at his hand. The dressing is turning red again.
He uses his working hand to clear a wire junction and calls three freight handlers by name. They arrive angry at being pulled from the ration line.
With the west route open, medics reach patients through a civilian-coordinated path, not a Fleet assault. Venn refuses an officer's proposed forced approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Not as long as repairing the consequences of shooting our way through a market that asked for doctors.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET — PRE-DAWN

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: The people who paid those men wanted the crowd angry.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: They found a crowd with good reasons already.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That's why it worked. They didn't have to persuade anyone that food was scarce. They just had to persuade them that somebody nearby had stolen all of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Your protected buyers will lose things they already paid for.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: They already have. I can stop pretending otherwise.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Do you know whether the man who paid the assassin is the same one who ordered the fire?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know they used overlapping accounts. If I say more than I can prove, somebody will use my mistake to make the entire record disappear.

panelPlan: PRE-DAWN. Jex sits at a scorched counter. The wound has been dressed. Naomi and the caregiver compare three independent pieces of evidence: the assassin's.
Jex makes the transaction ledger public while keeping private refuge routes redacted. He knows some honest customers will be financially injured by.
The caregiver points to a lost order.

*The caregiver points to a lost order.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: This one is mine. Medicine. Paid for before the attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I gave the access to emergency crews. Your consignment was moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I needed it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I can tell my patients the emergency crews needed the route. They know what an emergency is. But they're still going to need the drugs, and I have nothing to give them when they ask where they went.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'll reimburse the purchase.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: From whose account? The customers whose goods you cut through? The broker's reserve you just opened? You're running out of things that belong to you.

panelPlan: The caregiver doesn't leave. She turns the damaged payment chit toward Jex and makes him look at the shipment particulars. The medicines were purchased before.
Jex looks at the record. For the first time all night, there is something he can put right without pretending he can reverse the fire.

sourceActionBeats: *The caregiver doesn't leave. She turns the damaged payment chit toward Jex and makes him look at the shipment particulars. The medicines were purchased before any of the recent provocations. Their disappearance was a consequence of his rescue order, not of the assassin's plot.*
*Jex looks at the record. For the first time all night, there is something he can put right without pretending he can reverse the fire.*

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The loss is mine to report. The reimbursement comes from my own account. We can trace each consignment affected and ask the original buyer what would actually help. I won't make you discover the damage when you arrive at the next door.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: Don't make it another promise that needs a courier to explain why it's late.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No. I'll do the first one before you leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: I'm glad you opened the door. I'm angry that you didn't ask me. You're going to have to learn to live with both.

panelPlan: Naomi starts to offer help. Jex shakes his head. This is one task he intends to do himself while the caregiver watches the entry become real.
He has nothing clever to say. He gets out his own payment account and starts making the loss right where he can.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL — FEAR MASK / VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: We cannot recall every copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: Then we dispute the signatures. People will believe anything or nothing when they no longer know which page is original.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The signatures are genuine. We have copies ourselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: We are not deciding whether they are genuine. We are deciding which claim will be heard first.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The people in the market were there. Some of them helped carry the injured out. They don't need a ledger to know they were hungry and their neighbors were hurt.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: They need one to know who arranged it. Their own memories cannot tell them who paid an assassin. So they will listen to someone. The broker has made himself someone they might listen to.

panelPlan: The Fear Mask orders original authentication seals seized so the distributed copies can be challenged. The records have already moved beyond one vault.
The emissary waits, then risks an observation.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The Fear Mask orders original authentication seals seized so the distributed copies can be challenged. The records have already moved beyond one vault.*
*The emissary waits, then risks an observation.*

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: If we seize the original seals, they'll say the Triarch has something to hide.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: They already say that. What I want is time. An argument about the seals buys time.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: Time for what?

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: To learn which captains are moving food without asking us, and which couriers people trust more than our own officers. Start there. I don't need the market to admire us tomorrow. I need the people who want to replace us to find the work harder than they expected.

dialogueInline.speaker: MEDIC
dialogueInline.text: Are you family?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAREGIVER
dialogueInline.text: No. I found him in the smoke. His wife is on the other side of the market. I'd rather she hear he lived before she hears anything else.

panelPlan: The emissary takes the order. Nothing supernatural is involved: a political institution is attempting to exhaust the people challenging its account.
At dawn the caregiver leads an injured adult through Jex's sacrificed west passage to the waiting Fleet medics.
The medic helps the man onto a stretcher. Jex watches from the scorched corridor, holding a route token that says nothing about where Tali might be.
